card.title: The System Works
card.instruction: Celebrate every queue, delay, review, and formal approval as proof that a dependable system is protecting everyone from chaos.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our street-party application has reached a third committee. Reassuring to have so many safeguards.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The first two lost it. I need to book the tables today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And a third stands ready. One lost envelope can't plunge the street into chaos.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They want a fresh application. The table company won't hold our booking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good thing approval comes first. I'll reapply; you release the tables. Imagine seating everyone before we're protected.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 celebrates a third committee as safeguards, A3 treats lost applications as institutional redundancy, and A5 sacrifices the table booking to preserve approval-first protection.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's lost papers and booking deadline cause A3's third-committee reassurance; B4's restart requirement causes A5's reapplication and table release.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs practical equipment and B4 explains that the supplier cannot wait through the new approval cycle.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's costly conflict to affirm that protection must precede assembling the party.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a street-party application and multiple committees; B2-B4 state the real losses and deadline.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's imagine-seating-before-protection line grows from B4's tables rather than an unrelated institutional slogan.

coach2.situation: A1 establishes a street-party application and multiple committees; B2-B4 state the real losses and deadline.
coach2.stated: B4's fresh application follows the earlier losses; A5 explicitly releases, rather than claims to retain, the booking.
coach2.missing: No essential gap; the application outcome can remain pending because A chooses review over immediate preparation.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; formal delay is welcomed as dependable protection even when it imposes a concrete cost.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 corrects A1's many-safeguards account with lost applications and a deadline.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 reframes B2's losses as why another committee is reassuring.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 states the need to restart and the threatened table booking.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 chooses B4's reapplication over retaining the tables before approval.
